{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Roger David Nussbaum''' (born 29 January 1944, in [[Philadelphia]])<ref>biographical information from ''American Men and Women of Science'', Thomson Gale 2004</ref> is an American mathematician, specializing in nonlinear functional analysis and differential equations.

Nussbaum graduated in 1965 with a bachelor's degree from [[Harvard University]]. He received his Ph.D. in 1969 from the [[University of Chicago]] with thesis ''The Fixed Point Index and Fixed Point Theorems for K-Set Contractions'' supervised by [[Felix Browder]].<ref>{{MathGenealogyProject|id=6604|title=Roger David Nussbaum}}</ref> At [[Rutgers University]] Nussbaum became in 1969 an assistant professor, in 1973 an associate professor, and in 1977 a full professor. He retired there as professor emeritus.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roger D. Nussbaum|website=Mathematics Department, Rutgers University|url=http://www.math.rutgers.edu/~nussbaum/}}</ref> He was elected in 2012 a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].
